claims: Despite its hash.ts name, this unit contains no runtime code at all — every export is a type alias or a bare interface (Encoder included), so nothing in this file itself computes or produces a hash.

makeFixtureRepo writes a root .gitignore into every fixture that excludes everything under .atlas/ from version control except exactly .atlas/policy.json and .atlas/index.scip, so any other file placed in .atlas/ stays untracked by the fixture's git add -A commits.

No re-export in this barrel is selective: every statement is an unfiltered wildcard (`export *`), so anything exported by a listed sibling module becomes part of the package's public surface with no allow-list or renaming applied at this layer.

The module-private SEMANTIC_SLOTS array mirrors the SemanticSlot union by hand: its `readonly SemanticSlot[]` annotation guarantees each element is a legal slot but nothing enforces exhaustiveness, so widening the SemanticSlot type compiles cleanly while isSemanticSlot silently fails closed on the new slot until the array is updated too.

Because bodyAtom guards every body-character consumption with a negative lookahead against ANY_FAMILY_PREFIX — the union of all declared families' prefix sources, including the shape's own — a shape's greedy body run always halts at the first position where any family prefix could begin, so a match never absorbs the opening of another credential written immediately after it.

brand.js is the only module this barrel surfaces via an explicit hand-written named export list (asHash, asSubtreeHash, asNodeKey) rather than a star re-export, so any export added to brand.js itself will not appear at the package root until this list is edited.

Both Pack.invariants and Pack.advisory are declared with the identical element type readonly PackInvariant[], and PackInvariant carries no field marking which band a row belongs to (its tier is a bare, un-narrowed Tier), so the governing/advisory band separation is purely a producer-side convention that nothing in this contract's types actually enforces.

`undefined` is handled asymmetrically: as an object property value it is filtered out before serialization (so {a: undefined} canonicalizes like {}), but anywhere else it reaches serialize and is emitted as the literal null (so [undefined] canonicalizes byte-identically to [null]).

Through this barrel, `isSemanticSlot` is the only runtime value exposed from `./types.js` — the same module is also star-re-exported as type-only, so every other export of types.js reaches consumers of the package root as a type-only binding.

Territory is this module's sole declaration and export — no `seat` or `Glob` types are defined anywhere in the file — so `owner` and `globs` carry no nominal type safety beyond their bare `string` forms.

Within this barrel, './types.js' is the only module re-exported through the type-only form `export type *`; every other listed module is re-exported at runtime with plain `export *`, so the shared data model reaches consumers solely as erased types and adds nothing to the package's runtime surface.
isScope fails closed on the empty string: the guard requires v.length > 0 in addition to the typeof check, so '' is rejected even though the declared type predicate narrows only to plain string.

The `Grounding` interface's `entries` is a plain `readonly GroundingEntry[]`, so a receipt with zero entries type-checks fine — the non-empty requirement is not enforceable from this type, which is why the file additionally declares `isGrounded(g): boolean` as a separate runtime predicate.

In descentSteps, empty pieces produced by splitting a segment on '::' are kept as descent tokens — unlike empty slash-separated segments, which pathSegments filters out — so a malformed key like 'a/::/b' accumulates corrupted prefixes (e.g. 'a/::::/b') and is never normalized down to 'a/b' before exact-equality matching.

In writeDecision, the content-hash DEDUP check returns before nodeKey() is ever computed, so a candidate whose grounding would trigger DegenerateAnchorError is silently routed DEDUP instead of refused whenever its exact content already exists in the CAS.

Every import in this module is a type-only import and its sole exports are two interfaces, so the file contains no runtime values at all — nothing can be value-imported from it, and it compiles away to an empty module regardless of the type-level dependency on ./types.js.

cleanup() never throws: rmSync (with up to 10 retries at 100 ms delays) is wrapped in a try/catch that downgrades any removal failure to a console.warn, so a failed teardown cannot fail the test suite.

`createLog`'s `append` never verifies that an event's `id` matches its content-derived hash (`eventId`, defined in this same file); admission and deduplication key solely on the caller-supplied `id` string, so any structurally valid event is accepted under whatever id it carries.

`Fact` and `Ratified` are both declared as direct aliases of the very same imported type `GroundedFact`, so this unit's type system draws no distinction whatsoever between a machine-seeded fact and a human-ratified one — any function accepting one silently accepts the other, and enforcing the seeded-vs-ratified gate requires runtime checks or branding outside these declarations.

In `upsert`, refused writes surface as thrown errors rather than through the returned UpsertResult: a present-but-unrecognized slot throws `ClosedSlotError` before routing, and an UPDATE or SUPERSEDE that displaces an incumbent whose declared tier the write weakens or whose scope the write differs from throws `GovernanceAuthorityError` carrying a machine-readable `reason` field.

The branded Hash values minted here are produced solely by wrapping the output of bytesToHex(blake3(bytes)) in asHash, so their runtime value is the bare hex text of the digest with no prefix, envelope, or other metadata added anywhere in this file.

For any value produced by jsonObjArb, neither exclusion in hasNfcKeyCollision can ever fire — the KEY_TOKENS pool (a–d plus the é/ñ forms) cannot spell any of the three side-index names 'grounding', 'status', or 'freshness', and no arbitrary in this file generates undefined — so a true result on generated input always indicates a genuine NFC key collision, not a filtered-key artifact.

When canonicalization inside put throws, the method silently swallows the error and returns a single fixed module-level sentinel, EMPTY, which is literally the empty string branded as a Hash (asHash('')), so every kind of malformed input collapses into one value the Hash type cannot distinguish.

In makeCase, a drawn non-empty glue separator ('_' or '-') is silently skipped whenever pieceSafeAfter reports the still-open family's body would absorb its first character, so tokens inside a run can end up directly adjacent even on steps where a separator was chosen.

In the dependency axis built by dependencyAxis, every leaf node's subtreeHash is computed from the same value used as its key — the hashed file path produced by nodeHashOfPath/id({file}) — so those leaf hashes commit to nothing beyond the path string and are invariant under any change to the file's contents.

In both WriteRequest and CurrentNode, the `relationKind` and `shape` carriers are declared as bare `string`, even though sibling optional carriers like `slot`, `seal`, and `tier` are typed with imported domain types (`PredicateSlot`, `Seal`, `Tier`).

mergeNode never checks that its two arguments share a nodeKey — it reads only y.entries, and the returned node is labeled solely with x.nodeKey, so merging nodes from different nodeKeys silently absorbs y's entries under x's key.

In rehashPath, reaching the edited leaf is decided purely by depth (depth === pathKeys.length - 1) with no check of the reached node's key, so a mistyped interior segment of pathKeys that happens to match a real child silently applies newLeafHash to that wrong node and refolds all of its ancestors instead of failing.

In draftFact the tier argument never reaches the atlas draft subprocess — the argv is fixed to ['draft', anchor, slot, claim, '--json'] — and is instead stamped onto the parsed fact afterward via spread order, so the subprocess always runs with the CLI's own default tier.

All three retrieval modes return their facts ordered solely by a lexicographic sort of their content-addressed hash strings (after hash-based dedup inside the shared helper), so result order encodes no scope depth, dependency distance, or tag-list order, and identical queries always yield identical arrays.

The barrel contributes no declarations of its own and re-exports every runtime module wholesale via the unfiltered star form, with types.js as the sole module surfaced through a type-only re-export (`export type *`), so nothing in types.js can ever contribute a runtime binding to the package root.

The barrel re-exports a dedicated module for each of atlas-emit, atlas-reconcile, atlas-init, and atlas-query, yet despite its own annotations naming atlas-link as the second governed write door, its re-export list contains no link module at all, so the atlas-link write path cannot be located or reached through any link.ts-style module in this barrel.

In all three traversals (`propagateDirty`, `rehashState`, and free function `eagerRehashState`), the seed/edited node is placed into the visited set up front and is never itself processed, so it never receives a dirty bit, never appears in the eager re-hash list, and remains unresolved by its own `rehashState` call — only its dependents (within the hop bound) are affected, meaning `isDirty(node)` and `rStateResolved(node)` still return false for that exact node immediately after the calls.

In gitStoreProvenance's returned closure, a thrown runGit call caches 'trusted' before returning, so the very first query permanently latches the verdict — a transient git or exec failure sticks as the fail-open 'trusted' answer (propagating through any gitSidecarTrust built on it) for the closure's lifetime, with no retry.

The drift-eligibility registry is a fresh in-memory Set captured in each createCasIndex closure rather than anything derived from or persisted in the injected store, so two CasIndex instances built over the same StoreApi track eligibility independently, and recreating the index discards all prior registrations.

In this barrel, './types.js' is re-exported solely via the type-only statement ('export type *'), while each of the fifteen other modules (extract, admit-harness, admit-transition, admit-test-vacuity, cost-policy, align, seed, coverage, run-controller, loops, rank, usefulness, verify-fact, verify-count, verify-negation) is re-exported with value-level 'export *', so no runtime bindings from the shared data model ever reach the package root.

Despite its 'append' framing, admitToBuffer is not append-only: it discards the trailing provisional region of the previously returned buffer (known.back bytes, capped at MAX_SEAM_CARRY, or the widest window for a buffer it did not produce) and rebuilds that region from the re-decided carry, so the returned buffer's tail can differ from `existing` even before the new chunk's own bytes begin.

isT0Candidate flags a path only when one of its non-empty lowercased slash-separated segments exactly equals a T0_KEYWORDS entry, so names that merely contain a keyword (e.g. oauth, auth-plugin, payments-v2) do not flag.

Inside lineMerge, deduplication keys strictly on the raw parsed event's stored `id` property (first occurrence wins) and never invokes `eventId` to check that the id actually matches the content, so two events sharing an id silently keep only the earlier copy instead of surfacing a conflict.

Policy validation is all-or-nothing: a single malformed entry in the optional `anchors` map (e.g., an empty owner string) — or any invalid value in either top-level leg — makes parsing discard the entire policy, including all otherwise-valid scope declarations, and revert to the deny-all default.

In importCas, the re-hash/content-address verification (via addresses()) runs only on entries whose keys match the 64-char lowercase-hex HASH_SHAPE regex; any entry keyed otherwise is inserted into the returned store verbatim with no integrity check at all, so the 'fail closed' guarantee covers only hash-looking keys, not every entry in the bundle.

The refusal message renders the vocabulary list dynamically from the imported PREDICATE_SLOTS array, yet hard-codes the size in its own prose ('the closed 13', 'one of the 13', 'adding a fourteenth'), so nothing in this unit keeps the stated count in sync with the list it is printed beside.

Passing `indexerName` as anything other than the exact string 'scip-typescript' — including omitting `opts` entirely — leaves `opaqueRefSources()` permanently empty while `reverseCallers`, `holeSources`, `resolves`, and `definesAt` return identical results either way.

In createDiskStore's put, an input that fails either serialization — id(obj) throws, JSON.stringify(obj) throws, or stringify answers a non-string such as a bare top-level undefined — hits no filesystem call whatsoever and the method returns the one fixed sentinel hash EMPTY = asHash(''), so the returned Hash is not by itself proof that the object was stored.

In readSidecarSet, the corrupted-newest-generation fallback is unbounded: the loop retries every progressively older generation file from the full descending listGenerations output until one parses, and only after exhausting all of them does it consult the pre-protocol mirror — not merely the single previous generation that the unit's own prose ('one extra parse', 'the PREVIOUS generation') describes.

When the same global symbol is defined in more than one document, defDoc records only the first defining document in scip.documents array order, so a unit's own-versus-cross-unit classification of that symbol depends on document ordering rather than on the unit itself.

In runExtract's marginal-value halt, every non-emitted outcome — including a plain model abstention (null), a malformed-answer abstention, and a gate rejection — pushes false into the trailing-20 window, so a streak without any emitted fact stops the sweep before the budget ceiling is spent.
Within this module the concrete command client enforces only `budget.timeoutMs`; the `costCap` field of `LlmBudget` is declared but is never read by any code path here.

Despite its gate/token vocabulary, ratify's entire decision is two string comparisons on caller-supplied values: any non-empty token.by commits, with the sole extra requirement — applied only when the staged node's own tier property is exactly the string 'T0' — that token.by strictly equal the literal 'billy', so 'Billy', ' billy', or any other non-empty spelling commits nothing at T0 yet commits every other tier freely.

In createDepgraph's edge partition, an edge labeled kind === 'resolved' whose to is null fails the e.kind === 'resolved' && e.to !== null guard and falls into the else-branch, so its source is recorded in unresolvedSources exactly like an unresolved/dynamic edge and can set underApprox and union the coChanged band for scopes containing it.

The AST fold path (itemsOf, reached via foldAstUnits/foldAstUnitsWithPriors) parses the raw file content directly, so normalizeForGrammarGaps is applied only inside parseTsDoc — files carrying the three rescued constructs still fail closed to an unchanged tree under the fold.

For a git index entry with mode 120000, walkFileTree produces a leaf whose content is the stored link-target text fetched from the object database via `git cat-file blob <oid>` (after a /^[0-9a-f]{40,64}$/ charset check), and the symlink's on-disk target path is never opened — only non-symlink entries get their content from working-tree reads.

importMemory's fail-closed gate validates only the OKF envelope — the format literal is compared exactly, but version is merely type-checked as a number (any value passes, it is never compared to OKF_MEM_VERSION) and records are required only to be an array — then returns parsed.records verbatim without inspecting any individual record's contents.

Although both exported functions fold the same stored relation, `sameAsClassOf` never consults `sameAsRetracted` — unlike `deriveSameAs`, which filters its unions through `retractedPairs` — so an edge whose retraction is recorded still transitively widens the class `sameAsClassOf` returns.

decodeScipCached validates its memo entry solely by comparing the path's current stat mtimeMs and size against the values stored at the last successful decode — the bytes themselves are never hashed or compared for validation — so a rewrite of the dump that lands on the same mtime tick with an identical byte length will be served the previous decode from the cache.

In drift, an anchor that fails to resolve yields current === undefined, and staleness is computed as String(recorded) !== '', so a missing anchor is reported stale only when recorded is non-empty — e.g. drift('gone', '') returns stale: false.

In this unit's glob dialect the only wildcards are * (within one path segment) and ** (across separators); ?, [...], and {...} are backslash-escaped by escapeRe and therefore match only as literal characters.

Inside `put`, the returned hash and the stored bytes are derived entirely from `scrub(body)`'s output rather than from the caller's original argument, so the Hash addresses redacted content, not the body as offered.

Despite its documented pure-and-total, never-throw contract, isGrounded dereferences g.entries.length and each e.anchor unguarded (only subtreeHash gets a typeof guard), so a runtime-parsed grounding with nullish entries, a null element, or an anchor-less entry throws a TypeError out of driftDetect instead of failing closed to DRIFTED.

This barrel curates nothing: it contains no local declarations and no named re-exports — every statement, including the type line from './types.js', is a star-form re-export, so the package root's public surface is delegated wholesale to the individual source modules.

A territory with no matching tally in the frozen set — or whose tally has total === 0 — is given ratio 0 by ratioOf, so it passes gate() even at tier T0, meaning missing coverage data is silently treated as healthy rather than failing or throwing.

In classifyThrown, an untagged thrown Error whose name is not in the module's ENGINE_FAULTS set (the six JS engine error names) is classified as 'refused', not 'internal-fault', so a leg throwing a custom Error subclass for a genuine bug must tag itself via atlasFault or it files as a deliberate refusal.

Although RequiredAdvisoryField pins seven required fields, the executable code in this unit never reads 'owner' or 'scope' at all — hasRequiredFields checks only claimText and claimNorm as non-empty strings plus provenance and grounding as non-null, and validateTemplate adds only a byte-cap and slot-membership test, so neither field influences any reject/persist decision made here.

Inside admitPredicate, only the synthesized-check path gated by attest mints a kind:'predicate' node (via buildPredicate) — every other admitted route (a proven dependency/count/definition oracle, the type-expressible sound oracle, oracle abstention falling back through admitAbstainedAsJustified, and the no-synthesized-check semantic slot) returns a node built by buildSound/buildAdvisory/buildJustified and therefore carries kind:'advisory', several of them still wearing the LIKELY_INVARIANT label.

Containment is tested at any ancestry depth — the guard `segP.length < segQ.length` accepts any positive difference in `::`-segment count rather than exactly one level, and the all-ordered-pairs loop applies it uniformly, so a multi-hop chain produces an edge for every ancestor–descendant pair, not merely adjacent parent–child ones.

The structural graph argument is functionally inert: generatedOwner discards it with `void graph` and it appears nowhere else in reconcile's body, so passing any DepEdge[] — even an empty one — produces an identical OwnerMap.

This file's refusal vocabulary is a closed set of exactly three cases — contended, unreadable, and untrusted — enumerated as the complete key set of STAGING_REFUSAL_TEXT, which is typed as a total Record over the opaque imported CommitRefusal type, so any new refusal variant added upstream breaks this file's compilation until guidance text is supplied here.

In `route`, the stricter `strictestTier` join is applied only when the caller actually supplies `ctx.derivedTier`; if it is undefined, the ratification gate is decided solely by the candidate's own declared `tier`.

The `trusted` parameter is a zero-argument predicate function that isUntrustedStore invokes at call time (not a stored flag), and when the seam is undefined the predicate returns false, so a build without the provenance seam treats every store as trusted.

The derived atLeast counts every distinct referencing document in the caller set, including the defining unit's own references to its own export, because only the cross-unit eligibility check filters out self — the counting loop over callerSet never does.

When a relation row's `seal` is absent or not a string, the emitted edge object omits the `seal` key entirely (via conditional spread) rather than setting it to `undefined`, so key presence—not value—distinguishes sealed from unsealed edges.

In makeAlign, the deferred tail is silently discarded: interview() destructures only the capped batch and hands it to the injected ratifier in a single call, so open questions beyond the top-20 cap receive no ratification and produce no signal back to the caller.

unlinkSameAs performs no deletion: it appends the peer to each endpoint's separate sorted sameAsRetracted list while leaving every existing sameAs entry intact, so the assertion and its retraction coexist on the node rather than the edge disappearing.

The blastRadius in init's output is the exact array reference returned by index.blastRadius(path) — never copied or transformed — whereas each returned territory is a freshly constructed object built by spreading a raw territory with the 'T2' tier added.
The hot-set over-budget flag is computed with a strict greater-than comparison (size > budget), so a hot-set whose size exactly equals the budget is reported as not over budget.

If the optional freshnessOf callback is not supplied to negationsOf, every returned negation gets the literal freshness value 'DRIFTED', because the code coalesces a missing recompute to 'DRIFTED' rather than ever defaulting to 'FRESH'.

Each call of the assembled `upsert` port returns the entire cumulative grounded-fact set held in a closure-scoped Map — folded with every settled staging commit across the whole pass — not just the facts from the incoming batch being upserted.

Within createEmit's emit, the `at` hash is consumed only by the gate re-derivation check: the persisted object is `node` itself (cast to CasObject) and both the storage key and the returned id come from `id(node)`, so `at` never reaches the store or the output.

If any single citation's qualifiedPath fails to resolve, ground() immediately returns a brand-new { entries: [] }, discarding every entry already accumulated from earlier successfully-resolved citations, rather than dropping or skipping just the failed citation.

The fixed-point personalized PageRank discards the remainder at every integer division (each out-edge share, the dangling-mass redistribution, and both damping terms), and rank returns the raw accumulated scores divided by the 1e9 scale with no renormalization step, so the emitted ppr values are not a conserved probability distribution and need not sum to 1.

The two check legs parse their text asymmetrically in this unit: splitQuery takes everything after the FIRST '|' as the query's single argument (so a key containing a pipe survives intact in an index-query), while splitAssertion splits on EVERY '|', so the same piped key in an assertion yields extra parts and is refused by admit's exactly-three-parts check.

deserialize validates nothing beyond the parsed JSON being an object with a non-null object-valued `trailer` — every other Dossier field reaches the caller unchecked via the `as` casts, so an input like `{"trailer":{}}` is returned as a supposedly complete dossier.

In this barrel only source.js, reconstruct.js, and merge.js are re-exported via explicit named lists; the nine other runtime modules (provenance, attach, metering, host-adapter, placement, transcript-store, scrub, reinvoke, diff) are pulled in with blanket 'export *', so any symbol those files export automatically joins the package's public surface without an edit to this file.

The two legs of this fold use different equality semantics: the fact's own grounding-set subtreeHashes are compared positionally (so reordering the same hashes yields DRIFTED), while forward-closure members are compared as an order-independent, occurrence-counting multiset of node+interfaceRState keys (so reordering, or duplicating, the same members is decided by counts, not position).

Although the first parameter is named `candidate`, the gate never inspects it as a structure — coerceStatus requires the value itself to be exactly one of the four whitelisted strings ('HOLDS', 'BROKEN', 'NA', 'advisory'), so a structured candidate object, or any unrecognized value or casing, silently coerces to 'NA' rather than being examined.

In createGovernedEmit, the authorization and ratification gates are evaluated inside the callback handed to deps.store.commitProjection — alongside the incumbent lookup — while the shape and truth gates each run exactly once before that closure is ever entered.

In readCommit, a commit carrying an orchestra note but no trailer block still reads back as null, because deserializeDossier unconditionally returns null when the trailer text is missing — the JSON note alone can never reconstruct a Dossier.

crossesThreshold returns true for a territory with no served turns (whether unknown or registered-but-unserved) whenever the threshold argument is negative, because rateOf short-circuits to literal 0 and the predicate is a strict `>` over the unbounded number-typed OffAtlasThreshold parameter — so the no-served-history-yields-false behavior only actually holds for non-negative thresholds.

The binding is deliberately lossy: it keeps only a verdict strictly equal to the literal 'FRESH' and collapses every other oracle verdict — whatever non-FRESH states exist — into the single output 'DRIFTED', so any finer distinction the oracle reports can never be recovered from the returned freshness.

validateTemplate's entire body is just `typeof fact === 'object' && fact !== null && !Array.isArray(fact)` — it never reads any property, so a completely empty object {} (or any non-null, non-array value) passes, and no required-field or cap check exists anywhere in this unit.

In createGovernedStore, a write whose key already exists in the medium skips the set entirely yet still returns the guard's admitted verdict, so admitted:true cannot distinguish a fresh append from a duplicate no-op.

When ATLAS_MINE_SLOT is unset, resolveMineSlots returns exactly ['advisory', 'dependency', 'count'], so the two other valid arms ('definition' and 'semantic') are never mined by default and require an explicit selection.

`resolve` never reads its `seat` or `need` arguments — the returned `Resolution` (including `startedTier` and `direction`) is a pure function of `harness.canPropagateMcp` alone, so every pull need on a given harness resolves identically regardless of scope or seat.

In verifyDependency, the worldScope/holeSources test only chooses the abstain reason string ('scope-open' vs 'no-caller-in-scope') — both branches return the identical 'abstain' verdict, so worldScope can never upgrade an unwitnessed claim to any verdict other than abstain.

In commitLoop, a decision that returns the very projection object it was handed — reference-identical (===) to the durable head's projection — settles as successful with no file written at all, so a decide implementation that mutates the snapshot in place instead of rebinding to a fresh object would have its changes silently discarded.

All three imports in this file are type-only (`import type`), so the compiled module has zero runtime dependencies on @atlas/contracts, @atlas/grounding, or ../types.js — the real grounding predicate and hashing never execute from this file, making bindEmit's injected argument their sole runtime entry point.

Within this module the branded SubtreeHash is minted by passing encoder.hash's output straight through asSubtreeHash with no validation whatsoever — bindSubtree's body is a single expression with no length, encoding, or algorithm check — so nothing in this file constrains the digest's shape, and an injected stub encoder returning arbitrary strings would still satisfy the drift-oracle type.

In resolveCeiling, the drop loop only iterates kinds produced by orderDroppable, which excludes the pinned kinds 'awareness' and 'protocols.safetyCritical', so if the pinned injections alone exceed the ceiling nothing further can drop and the returned sum can exceed the ceiling.

In the bound implementation, supersede compares store.put(old)'s answer by strict equality against the local constant CAS_EMPTY ('') and throws a named UnaddressablePriorError on that one value instead of returning the {node, supersededBy} pair its signature promises — a throwing failure mode entirely invisible in the ArchiveApi surface.

Unrecognized config keys are neither rejected nor warned about anywhere in the loader, so a misspelled optional knob such as "timeoutMs" silently takes the provisional default (60 seconds) instead of being refused, even though a present-but-invalid value for the correctly spelled key throws.

A DriftItem's 'semantic'/'mechanical' class is decided solely by Set-membership of its fact id against the classifier's semantic list, with everything else defaulting to 'mechanical' — the classifier's mechanical list is never consulted for labelling, so the per-item labels and the returned mechanical/semantic arrays are derived through two independent paths.

In readAfterBareClone, the refspecConfigured argument gates only note lookups: a key found in the commit's trailer block is returned unconditionally before the note is ever consulted, so when the same key exists in both places the trailer value always shadows the note.

Although `factFor` is declared to return `Fact`, it fabricates the value from an ad-hoc object literal forced through an `as unknown as Fact` double cast, so the compiler never checks these fixture facts against `Fact`'s real shape and type drift in `Fact` will not surface here.

A failed `genesis` call assigns `pending = null` in its catch path, silently invalidating the closure-held checkpoint behind any resume token issued by an earlier partial run on the same controller instance, so a subsequent `resume` returns an empty degraded report instead of re-driving the remaining ranked sites.

In this unit surfaceBudget is a stateless constructor that returns hits: 0 and hitRate: 0 on every call and assigns a nonzero capTokens only to the 'projectMem' kind — the exported ORCH_TOK_CAP (800) is never referenced anywhere else in the file.

The sha validation in this unit is only a `typeof === 'string'` test — despite the `isHash` name and `v is Hash` predicate there is no length, charset, or content-address format check, so any string (including the empty string) passes the fail-closed gate and is forwarded unchanged to the injected source's diff.

In keyOf, the object passed to nodeKey is not the fact itself but { ...fact, slot }: the fact's own properties (including predicateSlot) are kept and a second, separate `slot` key — mirroring predicateSlot, or undefined — is injected into the view.

Although createPhaseHook accepts an optional pull port, onTransition never touches it (or the harness argument) — boundary delivery always re-materializes from the injected fresh-pack source — and even pullOptimize invokes the port only when the harness simultaneously reports nativePull === 'available', silently falling back to push materialization otherwise.

In verifyNegation, the counterexample search over reverseCallers(target) runs before the completeness check over holeSources()/opaqueRefSources(), so a 'refuted' verdict can be emitted even when the scope contains unresolved or collapsed references — scope hole-freeness gates only the 'proven' verdict and the 'scope-open' abstention (which therefore only occurs when no caller was witnessed).

In exact mode the closed-world gate tests reverse.holeSources() against worldScope while the witness count is taken under sourceScope, and nothing in this unit's body ties the two scopes together, so exact-mode soundness silently depends on the caller supplying a worldScope that covers sourceScope.

The fill() loop enforces the token cap identically on T0 and T1 candidates with no tier special-case, so when T0's own cumulative tokenEstimate exceeds the cap, the overflowing T0 candidates are pushed onto the pull-reachable tail alongside the truncated T1 rows rather than being guaranteed full inclusion.

Failed revs are not memoized: cache.set runs only after a successful build, so every later axesAt or reader call on a bad or retries-exhausted rev re-runs the entire throwaway-worktree checkout-build-teardown cycle instead of being served from cache.

Because ledgerSeededIds returns a set (never undefined) whenever coverage exists, seededCount yields 0 for a ledger containing no 'seeded' rows even when report.seeded is nonempty — the r.seeded.length fallback fires only when coverage is entirely undefined.

foldArchiveFromRecord projects only records whose kind is 'task', so an archive derived from a versioned record contains no 'pr' folds at all — meaning spawnRecall invoked with a 'pr' ResumeUnit against such an archive can never find a matching entry and will always throw.

The input to the seat-identity computation is decided by an unexported helper, briefOf, whose exhaustive branching means a bare-string record is used as-is, an object with a seatBrief key contributes only that field's value, and any other record contributes its entirety — so extra fields alter the seat input only for records lacking the seatBrief key.

Although VerifyReq includes a 'relation' arm and the leg returned by createVerifyFactLeg dispatches it to verifyRelation, verifyFactVerdict's kind whitelist covers only dependency/count/definition/negation and rejects 'relation' as an unknown kind, so no call routed through the shared verdict builder can ever reach the relation branch.

Inside poke(), the scope is added to the once-per-session poked set before the supplied pack and notice seams are invoked, so if either seam throws, the swallowed null return still permanently exhausts that scope's single poke for the session.

expandRound fabricates the Candidates it feeds back into propose→verify: each related site gets empty placeholder signals (the ZERO_SIGNALS literal) and a synthetic score of ppr = 1/(i + 1) with rank = position, so re-extraction runs on invented ranking data rather than any measured PPR or signals.

In reverifyRelation's pre-replay tamper checks, only endpointA is scope-bound to the witness (unitScopeOf(endpointA) must equal w.sourceScope); endpointB merely has to be a non-empty string whose file half names a document in the live index, with no scope relationship to the witness enforced before the oracle replay.

Even a fully readable SCIP dump causes buildTargetEscapes to return undefined unless the dump's metadata.toolInfo.name exactly equals the hardcoded string 'scip-typescript', so the leg silently degrades to the caller's fallback for any other indexer.
